newsitem.title: USA: CME peso futures volume on Thursday sets record.
newsitem.headline: CME peso futures volume on Thursday sets record.

text.p: Volume in Mexican peso futures at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange set a record high of 24,966 contracts on Thursday, nearly double its previous record of 13,235 contracts on February 15, 1996, the CME said.
Floor traders noted heavy selling on Thursday due to growing concerns about whether the U.S. administration would certify Mexico in its war on drugs.
They said one firm alone sold 2,500 March peso contracts. Each contract is worth 500,000 pesos.

On Friday, one floor trader said peso volume continued heavy as traders and dealers scrambled to cover short positions. Mexico's benchmark 48-hour peso was firmer against the dollar in midmorning trade on expectations the Banco de Mexico would intervene to bolster the peso.
He estimated that volume was 4,000 in March pesos and 2,500 in June pesos in the first two hours of pit trade.
Average daily volume in pesos in February, not including Friday, was 7,824 contracts, compared to January's average daily volume of 6,208 contracts.
Some said the market opened Thursday's session with a weak tone due to U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's comments in the first leg of his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday.
On the day Greenspan spoke, total open interest in CME peso futures set a record of 47,761.

Greenspan said he could not rule out the possibility of a pre-emptive tightening. The possibility of higher U.S. interest rates led some dealers and funds to shift assets out of Mexico and Latin America and into the U.S. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750;E-mail derivatives@reuters.com))
